title: Depth 4 -> 3 layers (2.4M params)
description: Same width and heads, one fewer block. About 1.3x more steps in 240 s and faster sampling in RL and eval.
hypothesis: Every run so far that trained fewer steps scored worse (003, 006, 007), and every timeout came from slow sampling. A shallower model gets more updates and samples faster; if 4 layers is more capacity than a cap-6 proof needs, this is a free win. Risk: not enough depth to do citation lookup + rule application.
surprise: 3000 steps, greedy 0.93 (same as baseline), sampling 750-870/s (fastest yet), but EI r1 solved 46 and eval 6. Greedy accuracy on cap-6 held-out is not predictive of the metric at all: 0.93 has produced 67, 56, 7 and 6.
